title: Packaged build orchestration and process identity controls
summary: Concurrent builds and event-driven runtime status are backed by persistent registries and process-identity revalidation.

dates.note: Exact project start/end dates remain unknown. Direct local source/history review on 2026-10-29 supplements the supplied October 5 snapshot and separately dated owner statements. Commit milestones and review dates are not project starts or release dates.

facts.text: Implemented concurrent packaged-module builds, persistent process registries, event-driven UI updates and production process controls in the engineering workbench.
Revalidated process IDs, start times and recorded executables before process-control actions; renderer readiness checks actual bundle assets rather than assuming a watcher means a completed build.
Added mocked IPC regressions and an opt-in live packaged test lane; the supplied analysis does not establish execution of that lane.

Made packaged-build monitoring recoverable by recording jobs before monitoring them, terminating a newly spawned build if registry persistence fails, resuming monitoring of recorded jobs after restart and broadcasting independent completion events.

notes: PID/start-time/executable revalidation reduces accidental process-control errors; it is not an OS sandbox or a proof eliminating every time-of-check/time-of-use race. Opt-in packaged test definitions were not run here.

Restart recovery reattaches monitoring to recorded jobs; it does not restart interrupted build commands or recover the original child exit status. Completion processing inspects the resulting module before registering it.
